purpose: Teach: 予見/告訴/蒸留/沈没/演算/概略/諜報/内政

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、災害を予見した古文書を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, I see you wrote your paper on ancient texts that predicted disasters.
lines.style: Warm, inviting tone. Gentle confirmation — she's read his work and wants to draw him out. Slight lift at the end, creating space for him to respond. Encouraging without pushing.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、名誉毀損の告訴事例を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, actually I wrote about a legal case involving defamation charges.
lines.style: Quiet correction, not argumentative. He's used to being misremembered and states the truth with calm precision. Slight pause before answering, gathering the right words.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、酒の蒸留技術史を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you covered the history of alcohol distillation technology in your paper, didn't you.
lines.style: Thoughtful, measured delivery. She's testing whether he'll correct her again, or perhaps genuinely reflecting on what she thought she remembered. Patient pause before the question.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、商船が沈没した事故の調査を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Actually, I researched the investigation into a merchant ship that sank.
lines.style: Polite but steady correction. He's not frustrated — this is familiar — but there's a quiet insistence on accuracy. Even tone, no defensiveness.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 演算理論の歴史を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: You wrote about the history of computational theory, didn't you.
lines.style: More engaged now, leaning in slightly. She's genuinely interested, though still testing or perhaps genuinely confused about his actual research focus. Conversational and warm.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、社会改革の概略を論文で扱いました
lines.en: No, I actually wrote about the outline of social reform movements.
lines.style: Mild weariness underneath the politeness. He's correcting for the third time. The words come easily but there's a thin line of something underneath — not anger, just a quiet recognition that she hasn't quite been listening.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、冷戦時代の諜報史を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you covered the history of Cold War espionage in your paper, I believe.
lines.style: Reflective, almost apologetic in tone now. She seems to sense his fatigue. The statement hangs a little, like she knows she might be wrong again but is genuinely trying to remember.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、近代国家の内政改革を論文で扱いました
lines.en: No — I wrote about internal political reforms in the modern nation-state.
lines.style: Final correction, delivered with polite resignation. His voice is quieter now, the earnestness worn thin by repetition. He's not angry, just accepting that the misunderstanding will continue.
